+# `logrus` Instrumentation
+
+This document explains how the `github.com/sirupsen/logrus` instrumentation provided by this repository works.
+
+## Overview
+
+`instrumentation/github.com/sirupsen/logrus` hooks `logrus.New`, `(*Entry).WithField`/`WithFields`, and `SetFormatter` to install a `logrus.Hook` that appends `trace_id`/`span_id` fields to log entries when an active span is available.
+
+## How trace/span ids are attached
+
+The installed hook calls `runtime.GetTraceAndSpanID()` (see `pkg/runtime/trace_context.go`), which returns the current goroutine's active trace/span id from goroutine-local storage (GLS), or two empty strings if none is available. If the returned trace id (or span id) is empty, the corresponding field is left off the entry.
+
+`GetTraceAndSpanID()` only returns real data once `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`'s own instrumentation (`instrumentation/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`) has registered its implementation via `runtime.RegisterTraceAndSpanIDFunc`. That registration only happens when `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` is applied — which, in turn, requires the package to be part of the application's build graph.
+
+## Limitation: `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` must be in the build graph
+
+**`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` must already be part of the application's build dependency graph (as seen by `go list -deps` / `go build -a -x -n`) for this instrumentation to inject `trace_id`/`span_id`.**
+
+Instrumentation imports declared in an `otel.instrumentation.go` file are tracked in `go.mod` but are intentionally **not** added to the build's dependency graph — that file is marked with the `//go:build tools` build tag specifically so instrumentation imports do not become build dependencies themselves. So relying on `logrus`'s own instrumentation module to pull in `sdk/trace` does not work.
+
+In practice, this means your application must construct a real `sdk/trace.TracerProvider` somewhere in its own source (for example via `sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(...)` and `otel.SetTracerProvider(...)`), even if you don't otherwise call the SDK directly. Without that, spans are still created and exported correctly, but `logrus` output will not carry `trace_id`/`span_id`.

Worth tightening this comment, because it currently reads as a resilience net and
invites a wrong assumption. With a non-nil `imports` map the fallback can never be
what produces a match:

- If the file imports this path unaliased, `importPathTail(path)` is already a key, so
  the lookup above **hits** and we never reach here.
- If the lookup misses, the key was derived wrongly — and this line compares against
  that same wrong tail, so it fails identically.

Since a successful tail comparison (`ident.Name == importPathTail(t.importPath)`) also
implies `ident.Name` is a map key, the map would always have hit first. So the only
case this branch actually serves is `imports == nil` (hand-built test nodes) — it is
*not* a safety net for imports the map keyed incorrectly, which is what "incomplete"
suggests.

```suggestion

		// tests with no backing *dst.File): compare against importPath's last
		// segment. Note this cannot rescue a mis-keyed map — a tail match here
		// would imply ident.Name is a key, so the lookup above would have hit.
		return importPathTail(t.importPath) == ident.Name && t.name == n.Sel.Name
```

doc says "Returns true when no sub-filters are set", which is exactly when the map is
pure waste. Rules with only `func:`/`recv:` pay a map allocation plus a walk of every
import for nothing.

It's already guarded by the cheap name+recv match so the cost is small; flagging it
because it's cheap to avoid, not because it's hot. Passing `root` and building the map
lazily inside `funcDeclMatchesFilters` (only once a filter needs it) would also drop a
